title: ns-next project
description: A Newspeak program of several modules, run by ns-next: `main` is the application's module, instantiated with `packageUsing:` a manifest of the others. Paths are relative to this file, with either separator.

$schema.description: Where an editor finds this schema; ns-next checks only that it is a string.

main.description: The application's module: its root class is instantiated with `packageUsing:` the manifest, then sent `main: platform args:`.

modules.description: The other modules the manifest holds, each asked for as `manifest at: '<id>'`, or `manifest at: '<id>' version: '<range>'`, by the id its source declares in `(* :module: <id>@<version> *)` above its class, or its class's name when it declares none. Two modules of one id must have two versions.

anyOf.description: The module's source file, and the id it is asked for by in place of the one it declares.

as.description: The module's id: identifiers separated by dots, the last its class's name, not beginning with `newspeak.`, which belongs to the modules ns-next ships. Its version stays the one the module declares.

scripts.description: Named command lines: `ns-next run --script <name>` and `ns-next bench --script <name>` hand one's arguments to `main:args:`, as if written after `--`; arguments after `--` follow them.

propertyNames.description: A script's name: not empty, and neither beginning nor ending with whitespace.

additionalProperties.description: A script: one string, split into arguments as a POSIX shell splits a command line, on every platform. Unquoted spaces, tabs and newlines separate arguments. '…' holds everything literally. Inside "…" a backslash escapes ", \, $, a backtick or a newline and is otherwise literal. Outside quotes a backslash escapes the next character. A backslash before a newline removes both. Adjacent parts make one argument; '' or "" alone is one empty argument. Nothing is expanded and nothing is an operator or a comment: $, *, ~, backticks, |, ;, &, (, ) and # are literal. An unterminated quote or a backslash at the end is refused.
